target.title: fix(update-check): wrap malformed npm view JSON parse in try/catch
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`fetchNpmPackageTargetStatus` bounds `npm view --json` stdout to 1 MiB, but malformed bounded output currently returns a raw `SyntaxError` string through the existing outer catch. Callers cannot tell that the failure came from npm metadata parsing.

## Why This Change Was Made

Wrap the parse at the metadata boundary with a contextual error while preserving the original parse error as `cause`. Keep the existing non-throwing API: callers still receive `{ version: null, nodeEngine: null, error }`. Focused coverage asserts that behavior; the earlier one-off proof script was removed from the production branch.

## User Impact

Update and status diagnostics distinguish malformed npm metadata from command execution failures without changing success or non-zero-exit behavior.

## Evidence

- Fresh structured autoreview on exact head `e4cd3b14d6f90478896e198cc6a3759809e619d6`: clean, patch correctness 0.98.
- Sanitized public/no-IAM AWS Crabbox `cbx_9bdddd960102`, run `run_5e3e3556b839`: passed a real child-process matrix using three executable fake npm binaries created on disk.
  - valid JSON: `version=1.2.3`, `nodeEngine=>=22.19`
  - malformed JSON: returned the contextual `npm view returned invalid JSON: SyntaxError...` error without throwing
  - non-zero exit: preserved `npm view failed: npm ERR! registry unavailable`
- Focused regression test remains in `src/infra/update-check.test.ts`; exact-head hosted CI is the merge gate.

Known scope: this improves diagnostics. The existing outer catch already prevented malformed npm JSON from crashing the update/status path.
